page: Vultr vc2-2c-4gb is a shared-core virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. Storage is bundled with 80 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate entry-level performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware, with scores of 1226.09 and 2501.8 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off from small-block cached reads at 176.23 GB/sec to large-block uncached reads at 19.26 GB/sec, which ranks in the bottom 10%. Database and application-level benchmarks reflect similar constraints, with Redis SET operations executing at 1.36 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 1.8 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vc2-2c-4gb offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can lead to resource contention and variable performance under sustained loads. Given the poor to weak benchmark ratings in CPU physics, encryption, and database operations, this instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, development environments, low-traffic staging servers, and simple automation scripts.
